newsitem.title: USA: Albright says Clinton to ask for China trade status.
newsitem.headline: Albright says Clinton to ask for China trade status.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton has decided to renew China's most favoured nation trading status for the coming year, Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Monday.
Clinton was expected to announce the move shortly, Albright said in a speech in Wilmington.

Congress has the right to overturn the decision to renew most favoured nation trading status for China. It begins debate on the issue next month, with opposition to renewal expected to be stronger than in past years.

Albright told a luncheon in this Delaware city attended by local business and political leaders that some in Congress would argue that a tougher line stood more chance of changing China's behaviour on human rights and arms exports.

But she said: "The administration's view is that our long-term interests are best served by a strategic dialogue with the Chinese leaders on a full range of issues...China with or without MFN status will be a rising force in world affairs."
